questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had wanted to go to Korea for a long time. It is different from my home country but easy to be in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university sends you all the information you need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university sends you informtion by mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used a website called goshipages, and texted different landlords and got a room through that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rooms are small but very survivable. Off campus housing is closer to public transport, and you can therefore get around the city faster. Getting to campus is easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a first-come-first serve system, where you have to compete for entry if there are too many who want the same course as you. Internet connection to Korea is not very fast, so you have to be fast and tactical about which courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university sent out a guide on how the course application process works, and there is also a test run so you can see how many are interested in different courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I had an interest in, while I was also tactical in regards to which courses that would get many applicants. Graduate courses dont get many applicants.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the test run and see how many are interested in different courses. The application starts at 8 (Korean time) so you have to be ready in the night to apply.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a poor selection of courses (in economics in English) and you dont know which courses will be available until July. In economics the courses are either beginner or PHD level, with only 1 being useful for a prioritized elective course in the bachelor programme for economics (in the autumn when I went on exchange).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied in difficulty. Even though the courses might have been hard to understand theoretically, they were easy to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures, no time in class to practice the material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding Asian Philosophy
Advanced Economic Theory
Topics In Microeconomics
Korean Language Program

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The korean language program is fun if you like to learn languages and really want to better understand Korea. But you have to pay extra to get the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to get a national health insurance unless you get the right insurance papers from you own insurance. There's also a lot of application fees for different things, they are small on their own, but there is plenty.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation is cheap, and can get cheaper the more you use it. Eating out is relatively cheaper than cooking for yourself, and you can eat out all the time. But you will still use more money on food than you could do at home if live cheap at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of clubs at the university, but the last date for application is before the semester starts for a lot of the clubs so you cant really apply for them. 
But at the university there is a "Buddy program", which you will be notified off, where you can meet other exchange students and Korean students, where there is a lot of different activities that you can partake in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around the city, and the towns around Seoul. You can easily get around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is different and you can make a lot of mistakes but you just have to keep calm. Physical awareness doesn't exist.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Calling waiters is very normal. Pickpocketting doesnt happen at all so people leave their phones and wallets at tables outside.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you know what courses can be available at "

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in a different country and eating Korean food.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness. Even though you meet a lot of people it takes time to get friends above surface level.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
